name: Cable Front Raise
description: The cable front raise is a shoulder isolation exercise using a low-pulley cable machine. The cable provides constant tension throughout the raising arc, unlike dumbbells which lose tension at the top of the movement. This makes it effective for targeting the anterior deltoid through the full range of motion, particularly at the top where the shoulder is at greatest challenge.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing away from a low-pulley cable machine, holding the handle(s) with an overhand grip at hip level. Stand upright with a slight forward lean and core braced.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a straight bar or rope or single handle to the low pulley. Stand with enough distance from the machine so the cable is taut at the bottom starting position.
steps: Step 1: Stand facing away from the cable machine, holding the handle at thigh level with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Keep the elbow slightly bent and the wrist neutral.
Step 3: Exhale and raise the arm(s) forward and up to approximately shoulder height or slightly above.
Step 4: Pause briefly, then inhale and slowly lower back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you raise the arm; inhale on the controlled lowering.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to generate momentum — keep the torso still
Raising past shoulder height into impingement territory for those with existing shoulder issues
safety_considerations: Stop the movement at or just above shoulder height unless mobility allows pain-free overhead reach
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise from hip level to just above shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Raise with a slight elbow bend — do not swing a stiff arm
Lead with the thumb side of the hand
